ai_technology: GPT-6.2; SolubleMPNN; specialized protein-model candidate filtering

evidence.ai_role: A prerelease GPT-6.2 generated proposed three-dimensional minibinder backbones from target structures through reasoning and general-purpose code; SolubleMPNN supplied sequences and specialized structure-prediction models filtered candidates before laboratory tests.
evidence.tested: The first-party announcement reports 35 binding-positive proteins among 322 laboratory-tested minibinders across five targets, based on GPT-6.2 backbone designs followed by specialized sequence generation and filtering. Onava was the study laboratory partner, not independent follow-up.
evidence.unknown: The linked preprint Methods were not read in this review; detailed assay conditions and binding thresholds were not assessed. Binding does not establish specificity, useful biological activity, safety or therapeutic efficacy. End-to-end design without specialized-model assistance and independent replication are not established.

source_review.scope: Full first-party OpenAI announcement, including laboratory workflow, measured hit counts and limitations. Linked 89 MB preprint exceeded the web reader limit and its Methods were not read.

summary: OpenAI reports that Onava laboratory tests found binding for 35 of 322 minibinders based on GPT-6.2-designed structures, with at least one hit for each of five targets. GPT-6.2 generated backbone designs using reasoning and general-purpose code, while SolubleMPNN supplied sequences and specialized models helped select candidates. The November 24, 2026 announcement links a preprint; the findings do not establish an end-to-end workflow without specialized models, independent replication, specificity, therapeutic activity or clinical benefit.
title: GPT-6.2 protein designs show binding across five targets in laboratory tests
